title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π = Π_{0,3}^∧ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 \ {0,1,∞}, topologically free on two generators. Its three inertia generators are l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. The page uses an S_3-type symmetry of it: ρ is an order-3 automorphism permuting l_0 → l_1 → l_∞ cyclically, and σ_∞ is an order-2 automorphism exchanging l_0 and l_1. These are realised inside an enlarged group (Π^~ = Π·{1, ε_0}, presumably Π extended by these symmetries; the exact definition is on earlier pages).

M_{0,3}^{!~} is the group of automorphisms u of this extended structure that respect the inertia classes (the '!') and the symmetry elements up to Π. Each such u is encoded by a 'cocycle' pair (g, h) of elements of Π, via (117):
- u(ρ) = gρ;
- u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞.

The conditions (116). Since ρ^3 = 1 and σ_∞^2 = 1 must be preserved, one needs g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 and h σ_∞(h) = 1. The compatibility of the two symmetries forces g = h · l_1^ν for some ν in Ẑ (the '(ν ∈ Ẑ conv.)' means for a suitable ν).

The coboundary form. One may write g = α ρ(α)^{-1} and h = β σ_∞(β)^{-1}. Then u acts on the symmetry elements by conjugation, as stated in (118). Under this substitution, (116) becomes the 'sempiternelle relation des lacets' α ρ(α)^{-1} = (β σ_∞(β)^{-1}) · l_1^ν.

The marginal note is the key methodological statement: 'In all this I drop the loop equation and restrict myself to the relations (116) on Π_{0,3}.' In other words, he passes from the full 'loop equation' to just the order-3 (cyclic) and order-2 (inversion) cocycle relations. In modern terms these are the 3-cycle (hexagon-type) and 2-cycle relations that define GT-hat, without the pentagon.

The subgroup [0]. M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] is the subgroup of u normalising the inertia group L_0 = l_0^{Ẑ} (defined on the previous page).
- (119): its intersection with the inner automorphisms Π is exactly L_0.
- (120)–(122): the inclusion Ẑ ≅ L_0 → M is explicit. For λ = l_0^n, int(λ) corresponds to α = β = λ and g = h = λ ρ(λ)^{-1} = λ σ_∞(λ)^{-1} = l_0^n l_1^{-n}, with ν = 0.
- (123)–(124): left multiplication by λ acts by (α, β) ↦ (l_0^n α, l_0^n β) and (g, h) ↦ (l_0^n g l_1^{-n}, l_0^n h l_1^{-n}).
- These agree with the cocycle composition law (125) on the next page: g'' = u'(g) g' and α'' = u'(α) α'.

Where it leads. The next page divides out by L_0 to get N_{0,3}^{!~} = M[0]/L_0, described as pairs (α, β) satisfying the loop relation, modulo (α, β) ~ (l_0^n α, l_0^n β). This is a normalised automorphism group of the profinite free group of rank 2 cut out by S_3-symmetry cocycle relations. It is a close relative of (a 'two- and three-cycle only' version of) the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT-hat later defined by Drinfeld and Ihara.
errors: (118) looks swapped. From (116)–(117), u(ρ) = gρ = α ρ(α)^{-1} ρ = int(α)ρ and u(σ_∞) = int(β)σ_∞. The page instead writes u(σ_∞) = int(α)σ_∞, u(ρ) = int(β)ρ: either a slip, or the letters are attached the other way round from line 2.

In (122) the second component reads l_0^{-n} l_1^{-n} (as transcribed). For int(l_0^n) both components must equal l_0^n l_1^{-n}, which is what the following line 'f = g = λσ_∞(λ)^{-1} = λρ(λ)^{-1}' asserts. The variable names also switch from (g, h) to (f, g).
(124) uses (ξ, η) for the pair that (116)/(117) call (g, h); this is notational drift rather than a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Encoding automorphisms of the profinite π1 of P^1 minus 3 points, compatible with the S_3 symmetries ρ (order 3) and σ_∞ (order 2), by cocycle pairs (g, h) with gρ(g)ρ²(g) = 1, hσ_∞(h) = 1, g = h l_1^ν.
ideas.modern_name: 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT-hat; cocycle description of GT elements (λ, f)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the Teichmüller tower and GT-type relations only qualitatively; these explicit formulas appear unpublished.

ideas.what: Deliberately dropping the full 'loop equation' and studying the group cut out by the order-2/order-3 relations alone.
ideas.modern_name: Groups defined by GT relations without the pentagon (cf. Lochak–Schneps 'GT^' variants, Ihara's group of automorphisms commuting with S_3 symmetries)

ideas.what: Subgroup normalising inertia L_0, its intersection with inner automorphisms being L_0 ≅ Ẑ, and the explicit action of L_0 on (α, β) and (g, h).
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of GT elements modulo inner automorphisms by inertia (the standard normalisation f ∈ [F̂_2, F̂_2])

missed.claim: This is an explicit 1980s cocycle presentation of the S_3-symmetric automorphism group of π̂_1(P^1 \ {0,1,∞}), essentially the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT-hat. Grothendieck explicitly isolates these relations from the 'loop equation'. It documents that he had the defining relations of GT-hat in group-cocycle form years before Drinfeld.
missed.quote: Dans tout ceci, je laisse tomber l'«équation des lacets», et me borne aux relations (116) sur Π_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context for GT. The variant with only the (116) relations, normalised by inertia at 0, is a natural intermediate group whose comparison with GT-hat is studied only sporadically.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows GT-type relations in cocycle form with S_3-symmetry bookkeeping, which is notable as a historical precursor. However, Grothendieck's anticipation of GT is widely acknowledged. The computations themselves (inner automorphisms by l_0^n, cocycle law) are routine, and the relations are standard since Drinfeld/Ihara.
transcription_corrections: (121) probably reads λ = l_0^n ↦ (α = λ, β = λ), with marks indicating which symmetry (ρ, σ_∞) each refers to; the transcribed exponents 'λ_ρ^ξ', 'λ^∞' are doubtful.
(122) second component is likely intended as l_0^n l_1^{-n} (it is consistent with 'f = g = λσ_∞(λ)^{-1}'); the variables are f, g on the page rather than g, h.
Line 2: 'β σ_∞(β)^{-1}' — the image shows an overwritten σ_∞ (or τ_∞); the next page writes τ̄_0, suggesting fluctuating notation.
